title: First aid basics (signpost)
examples: If someone faints, what is the first thing I should do?
How do I put an injured person in the recovery position?
What numbers should I call in an emergency?

explain.say: When you find someone who is unwell, your first job is to check the scene.
Next, you must check if the person is awake and breathing normally.
If they are breathing but unconscious, you should place them in the recovery position.
If they are not breathing, you must call emergency services right away.
If you are alone, call for help and then check the person's condition.
In a real emergency, always remember to check for danger before helping anyone.

faq.q: What is the very first thing I should do when I find an injured person?
faq.a: You must first check the scene to make sure it is safe for you to approach. You should never become a second casualty.
asks: Should I check for danger first?
What is the priority when helping someone?

faq.q: How do I put someone in the recovery position?
faq.a: You gently roll the person onto their side, keeping their head supported and their airway open. This helps keep the tongue from blocking the airway.
asks: What is the recovery position for?
How do I keep an unconscious person safe?

faq.q: What number should I call for help in an emergency?
faq.a: You should call the local emergency services number, such as 999 or 911. They will send trained medical help to your location.
asks: What is the emergency phone number?
Who do I call if something bad happens?

faq.q: If the person is breathing, do I need to do anything else?
faq.a: If they are breathing normally, you should place them in the recovery position. This keeps their airway open until medical help arrives.
asks: What if they are breathing but unconscious?
Is the recovery position always needed?

faq.q: What information should I give to the emergency operator?
faq.a: You must clearly state your exact location and what the emergency is. This helps them send the right help quickly.
asks: What details do I need to know?
What should I tell the person on the phone?

facts: Always check the scene for danger before giving first aid.
The recovery position is used for an unconscious person who is breathing.
If the person is not breathing, call emergency services immediately.
When calling emergency services, stay calm and speak clearly.

quiz.say: Before touching an injured person, you must first check:
quiz.why: Checking the scene first keeps you safe so you can help others.

wrong.0: You must check safety regardless of if they are conscious.
wrong.2: This is the second step; you must check safety first.
wrong.3: You cannot check injuries if the area is unsafe.

quiz.say: If an unconscious person is breathing, they should be placed in:
quiz.why: This position keeps the airway open and prevents choking.

wrong.0: This can allow the tongue to block the airway.
wrong.1: This position does not keep the airway open properly.
wrong.3: Sitting can cause the airway to collapse if the person is unconscious.

quiz.say: If you call emergency services, what is most important to tell them?

options.show: How badly the person is hurt
options.say: How badly the person is hurt

quiz.why: Knowing where you are helps the ambulance get to you fastest.

wrong.0: While important, location is needed first for them to start coming.
wrong.1: This is helpful, but location is the most immediate need.
wrong.2: This detail is not necessary for emergency services to help.
